reports.name: Ching-Hsien Ko
reports.peak_summary: Projection: bench or platoon bat with medium risk. The current bat shape is impact over 243 PA.
reports.published_report: Ching-Hsien Ko is a high-strikeout left-handed hitter who controls the strike zone far better than his age cohort, building on-base skill that projects ahead of power development. His current minor-league line shows a .416 OBP and 17.3% walk rate—both elite for a 19-year-old at A-ball—but the 25.5% strikeout rate and .195 ISO hint at a player still learning to do consistent damage; when translated to the majors, his strikeout rate ticks to 28.8% while power erodes further to .132 ISO. The main risk is that his contact approach may not translate into average power, leaving him capped as a low-run-production bench option even if the discipline holds. The current 243 PA sample is fresh and substantial enough to trust the walk rate, but the connection between walk ability and future value depends entirely on whether he closes the power gap against advanced pitching.

reports.name: Stiven Martinez
reports.peak_summary: Projection: organizational depth with medium risk. The current bat shape is mixed over 192 PA.
reports.published_report: Stiven Martinez is an 18-year-old center fielder swinging and missing at an alarming rate while generating just enough power to stay off the floor. His 35.9% strikeout rate ranks in the 6th percentile—well above league norms even accounting for his age and level—and has dragged his .297 OBP and .686 OPS to the bottom third of the prospect pool despite respectable ISO at .155 (55th percentile). The core risk is contact; strikeout discipline this severe at age 18 in A-ball is the kind of hole that doesn't close on its own without radical mechanical or approach changes. Sample is current and clean at 192 PA, but one season is insufficient to know if he can tighten the strike zone.
